title: ThriftScout
tagline: The world is your thrift store: say what you want, and scouts already thrifting keep an eye out.
stateNote: A live no-card pilot with real accounts. No payments or payouts are collected yet.
problem: Good finds sit in thrift stores where the people who want them never see them. ThriftScout connects buyers, scouts who are already in the aisles, and the stores themselves.
audience: Thrift shoppers, people who thrift for others, and thrift stores.
contribution: It is my project, built with Next.js and Supabase. The source is private.
worksToday: Browse finds, post a wanted request, or run a price check, as shown on the live site.
Scouts can post finds from a store.
Real accounts work across devices in the pilot.
limitations: No card payments or payouts are collected yet.
The store listed is an unclaimed scout location, not a verified partner.

involve.headline: Run a thrift store, or thrift a lot?
asks: If you run a thrift store and want to try it, tell me.
Tell me what you'd want a scout to find for you.

disclosure.note: The owner stated on 2026-10-29 that ThriftScout should have serious visibility. The source stays private; this page describes only the public site's behavior and its stated limits.

approach: Built as a web app with Next.js and Supabase so buyers, scouts and stores share one system across devices.
Three entry points match the three sides of the marketplace: browse finds, post a wanted request, or post a find from a store.
Launched as a live pilot with real accounts before taking any money.

decisions.why: Real accounts and real use come before payments and payouts, so the marketplace can be tested without anyone's money at stake.
A store a scout adds is shown as an unclaimed scout location, not presented as a verified partner.

caseStudy.source: the project details above and the hosted build (checked 2026-10-29).
